newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: PLDT sees positive response to debt float.
newsitem.headline: PLDT sees positive response to debt float.

text.p: Philippine Long Distance Telephone Co (PLDT) is expecting a favourable response to its $200-million bond issue this month, a company official said on Thursday.

"We are riding on positive sentiments on the country's economic prospects. This is a very good time for Philippine companies to issue debt securities overseas," PLDT executive vice president Edgardo del Fonso told Reuters.

Moody's Investors Service announced last month that it was placing in review for possible upgrade the Ba2 foreign currency sovereign ceiling for bonds and notes of the Republic of the Philippines, as well as the country's Ba3 foreign currency sovereign ceiling for bank deposits.
PLDT is currently rated with the sovereign at Ba2 by Moody's and BB by Standard and Poor's Corp.
Del Fonso said PLDT is set to conduct a "road show" for its bond issue in Hong Kong next week.
"After Hong Kong, we will go to other financial centres like London and the United States," del Fonso said.
"We have yet to decide on the maturity and the yield of the issue. It may likely be straight bonds with at least 10 years maturity," del Fonso said.
